description: This is a modern 'Nodes View' dashboard for your Kubernetes cluster(s). Made for kube-prometheus-stack and take advantage of the latest Grafana features. GitHub repository: https://github.com/dotdc/grafana-dashboards-kubernetes Adapted from dotdc/grafana-dashboards-kubernetes (Apache-2.0, https://github.com/dotdc/grafana-dashboards-kubernetes); modified. See THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

panels.title: CPU  Usage
panels.description: CPU busy on the selected node, as a share of its cores (idle, iowait and steal excluded). Sustained above 70% means the node is short of CPU: move work off it or add nodes.

panels.title: RAM Usage
panels.description: Memory in use on the selected node (total less available), as a share of its RAM. Sustained above 80% means eviction risk on this node.

panels.title: Pods on node
panels.description: Pods scheduled on the selected node. Compare with the node's pod limit.

panels.title: List of pods on node ($node)
panels.description: Every pod scheduled on the selected node, with its namespace and phase. Use it to find what to drain or move.

panels.title: CPU Used
panels.description: CPU cores busy on the selected node right now.

panels.title: CPU Total
panels.description: CPU cores the selected node has.

panels.title: RAM Used
panels.description: Memory in use on the selected node right now (total less available).

panels.title: RAM Total
panels.description: RAM the selected node has.

panels.title: uptime
panels.description: Time since the selected node booted. A short uptime with no planned replacement means it restarted: look for a crash or a spot reclaim.

panels.title: CPU Usage
panels.description: CPU time on the selected node by mode. A tall `iowait` is a slow disk, `steal` is a noisy neighbour on the hypervisor, `system` is the kernel (network or syscalls).

panels.title: Memory Usage
panels.description: Memory on the selected node split into used, buffers, cache and free. Free near zero is normal; available falling toward zero is not.

panels.title: CPU usage by Pod
panels.description: CPU cores used per pod in the selected namespaces. Click a series to open the pod, and compare with its requests and limits there.

panels.title: Memory usage by Pod
panels.description: Working-set memory per pod in the selected namespaces. A climbing line is a leak; click a series to open the pod.

panels.title: System Load
panels.description: Load average over 1, 5 and 15 minutes on the selected node. Sustained above the node's core count means work is queueing for the CPU.

panels.title: Context Switches & Interrupts
panels.description: Context switches and interrupts per second on the selected node. A jump with no traffic change points at a runaway process or a failing device.

panels.title: File Descriptors
panels.description: File descriptors allocated against the node's maximum. Near the maximum, processes start failing to open files and sockets.

panels.title: Time Sync
panels.description: The kernel's estimated and maximum clock error on the selected node. Growing error means the node is losing time sync: certificates and tokens start to fail.

panels.title: Network usage (bytes/s)
panels.description: Bytes per second received and sent on the selected node's real interfaces (pod interfaces are left out). Compare with the instance's network limit.

panels.title: Network errors
panels.description: Receive and transmit errors per second on the selected node. Above zero points at a faulty interface, driver or cable.

panels.title: Network usage (packet/s)
panels.description: Packets per second received and sent on the selected node.

panels.title: Network total drops
panels.description: Packets dropped per second on the selected node. Above zero means saturation of the interface or its queues.

panels.title: TCP Currently Established
panels.description: TCP connections established on the selected node. A climb with no traffic change is a connection leak.

targets.expr: max(kubelet_volume_stats_used_bytes{node="$node", k8s_cluster_name="$cluster"}) by (persistentvolumeclaim, namespace) / max(kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_bytes{node="$node", k8s_cluster_name="$cluster"}) by (persistentvolumeclaim, namespace)

panels.title: Persistent Volumes - Usage in %
panels.description: Used share of each persistent volume mounted on the selected node. Above 85% means the volume is close to full: expand it or clean it.

panels.title: Persistent Volumes - Usage in GB
panels.description: Used, free and total bytes of each persistent volume mounted on the selected node.

panels.title: Persistent Volumes - Inodes
panels.description: Used inodes as a share of capacity per volume. Running out of inodes stops writes even with free space: clean up small files.

panels.title: FS usage in %
panels.description: Used share of each filesystem on the selected node. Above 85% on the root or the container runtime's disk means the node is close to evicting pods for disk pressure.

panels.title: FS inode usage in %
panels.description: Used share of inodes on each filesystem of the selected node. Near 100% the disk refuses new files while still showing free space.

panels.title: Reads by disk (bytes)
panels.description: Bytes per second read from each disk of the selected node.

panels.title: Writes by disk (bytes)
panels.description: Bytes per second written to each disk of the selected node.

panels.title: Completed reads by disk
panels.description: Read operations per second completed on each disk of the selected node. Compare with the volume's provisioned IOPS.

panels.title: Completed writes by disk
panels.description: Write operations per second completed on each disk of the selected node. Compare with the volume's provisioned IOPS.

panels.title: Disk(s) io/s
panels.description: Operations in flight on each disk of the selected node. A queue that stays above a few means the disk is the bottleneck.

panels.title: FS - Device Errors
panels.description: Filesystems on the selected node that could not be read (1 is an error). Any value above zero is a mount that is broken or gone.
